text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV rose in heavy trade on Thursday to highlight a sagging market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said ADRs were hit by concerns about possible increased U.S. interest rates after the government reported better-than-expected retail sales for February.
Decliners led advancers by 307 to 187 among 806 ADRs, and the sector was off 0.39 percent at midday. Volume was 34 million shares.
"Good news for the market now is met with an, 'OK, fine,'" a trader said. "Bad news is met with, 'I'd better get out of here, I'd better get some profits.'"
CANTV, an acronym for Compania Anonima Nacional Telefonos de Venezuela, rose 1-5/8 to 28-7/8 as company workers struck in a wage dispute. Volume was a heavy 690,500 shares.
The shares were boosted by initiation of Credit Lyonnais' start of coverage. The firm rated CANTV a buy.
SBC Warburg also recommended the stock, saying a recent slump in the price created a buying opportunity.
Swedish telecommunications equipment maker LM Ericsson rose 7/8 to 35. Canadian gold mining company Bre-X Minerals eased 1/16 to 12-3/4 in heavy trade.

Mexican ADRs were weighed by uncertainties about whether the U.S. House of Representatives would overturn President Bill Clinton's certification of Mexico as an ally in the effort against drug trafficking.
Mexican bellwether Telefonos de Mexico fell 1/4 to 39-1/4 in moderate trade.
